newsitem.title: POLAND: OSCE monitors approve Macedonian municipal polls.
newsitem.headline: OSCE monitors approve Macedonian municipal polls.

text.p: OSCE observers of the first round of municipal elections in Macedonia said it found few flaws in the November 17 polls apart from problems with voter registration.
The Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) monitors said in a statement that 89 percent of voters asked felt the voting process was conducted properly.
The statement was released in Warsaw by the Office for Democratic Institutions and Human Rights (ODIHR) which coordinates OSCE international monitoring of elections.

"The information gathered and the friendly contacts we have had throughout, at all levels of the local elections, give us an optimistic outlook on the development of the country's democratic future," the OSCE statement said.
It said observers were told by party officials present at the stations that in some cases 10-20 percent of voters were not registered, but said such a statement could not be "scientifically precise".
European Union observers monitoring local elections in the former Yugoslav republic said on Monday that 25 percent of voters could not cast their ballots because they were not on electoral lists.

"Presidents of local boards on a large number of occasions acknowledged that there were deficiencies in the register whilst reporting much lower and more plausible estimates of discrepancies," the statement said.
Macedonians voted in 124 municipalities across the country on Sunday in a poll analysts said would shape the future of the country's national politics.

Partial returns showed Macedonian opposition parties leading the ruling Social Democrats in several major towns, although some 90 percent of councils appeared certain to need a second round of voting to decide the eventual outcome.
